title: Reconnect handshake handoff and server lease refresh for resilient streaming
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: production services experience intermittent client disconnects (mobile flaps, network handovers). Existing streaming behavior loses in-flight toolcall/state and forces full retry which causes duplicate side-effects and poor UX. This PR introduces a lightweight reconnection handshake with explicit handoff semantics, a short-lived server lease for inflight sessions, and a soft-lease refresh path so reconnecting clients can resume streaming without replaying side-effectful tool calls. It also updates the OpenAI compatibility adapter to surface reconnection metadata for clients and adds idempotency enforcement hooks for tool/function calls.

Design summary: 1) handshake: when a client reconnects within a configured grace window it provides prior_session_id + reconnect_token. Server validates token and either returns a resume_ack (session reattached) or a replay_hint (client should replay prompt but mark toolcalls idempotent). 2) server lease: newly-created streaming sessions allocate a short-lived lease (default 45s) that preserves in-memory KV for quick reconnects; background TTL refresh can extend leases for healthy sessions. 3) handoff semantics: if a reconnecting client attaches while a worker is mid-toolcall, the server sets a toolcall-escrow flag and returns a toolcall-status block in the resume_ack so the client can safely decide to wait, replay with idempotency token, or soft-abort (no-op). 4) OpenAI-compat adapter exposes X-Redwood-Reconnect-Token and Reconnect-Window headers and maps resume_ack -> delta events for streaming consumers. 5) Structured output integrity: partial JSON chunks are repaired by the runtime on resume by replaying remaining tokens from the point-of-truth (server-side reconstruction), avoiding malformed outputs on client reconnect.

Checklist (completed): - [x] runtime: reconnection handler, lease manager, token validation - [x] API: header + body compatibility changes, resume_ack schema - [x] sdk-python: reconnect helper + examples - [x] openai-adapter: header mapping and migration tests - [x] e2e: integration test with simulated disconnects and mid-toolcall reconnection - [x] docs: short migration note and example flow in console docs

Risk/rollout notes: default behavior is backward compatible: clients that do not send reconnect metadata get existing semantics. Feature gated by runtime flag stream.reconnect.enabled=false for canary rollout. Idempotency tokens for toolcalls are required only when toolcall is marked side-effectful; we added a runtime check and a developer warning in logs for missing tokens.

Related: ENG-3187 (reconnect product spec), ENG-3201 (toolcall idempotency), incident INT-442 (customer outage reproducer).
